desc:
AI prompt guides with examples help your team ask for what they need and get usable answers. Ecom Swift LLC writes a guide in your own business language, with copy-ready prompts for the tasks your team does every week.

## What is a prompt guide?

A prompt guide is a short reference document that shows people how to word requests to an AI tool and gives ready examples for their daily tasks. Each example has the prompt itself, a sample result and a note on what to check before the result is used.

The guide is written for your business, with your tone, your product names and your usual customers, so it feels like part of the job and not like a general lesson.

## Why vague requests produce weak answers

An AI tool answers what it is asked. If the request is vague, the answer is vague. Asking for a supplier email gives a generic email. Asking for a polite, firm reminder to a supplier who is late with a specific order, in two short paragraphs, in your usual friendly tone, gives something you can almost send.

Most people never learn this because nobody shows them. They try once, get a mediocre result, and decide the tool is not useful. A guide closes that gap in an afternoon.

## How good prompts save time

Good prompts reduce rewriting. The first draft lands closer to what you wanted, so editing takes minutes and not a second attempt. Across a week of emails, product notes, social posts and meeting summaries, that adds up to meaningful hours for the person doing them.

The mechanism is context. A prompt that states the goal, the reader, the tone, the length and the facts to include leaves little room for guessing. A fill-in template makes this repeatable, so a new team member gets the same quality on day one. Results still need a human check, which is why every example includes one.

## What a great prompt guide includes

- A handful of clear rules for asking well, in plain words.
- Prompts grouped by task, such as email, product text, social posts and summaries.
- A sample result for each prompt, so people know what good looks like.
- A short check list of what to verify before using the output.
- Fill-in-the-blank templates for the tasks done most often.
- Your tone of voice and common terms built into the examples.
- A list of common mistakes and how to fix them.
- Notes on what never to paste, such as customer details.
- An editable document format, so your team can add its own prompts.
- Role tags, so people can find the prompts for their job quickly.

## How we write your guide

We start by learning your tasks. You tell us what your team writes, summarizes and answers each week, and we ask for a few real examples with private details removed. We write the prompts, test them on a common AI chat tool and refine them until the results are consistent.

The Basic package provides a short guide with copy-ready prompts, sample results and a check list. Standard adds prompts organized by task group, fill-in templates, your tone and terms and a list of common mistakes. Premium delivers a full library for your team, with role tags, prompts for your own tools, a short recorded walkthrough and an update after a month of use. Add-ons include extra prompts, a one page cheat sheet and a session where your team tests the prompts together.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- State the goal, the reader and the tone in every prompt.
- Give the tool the facts it needs, and ask it to use only those.
- Ask for one clear format, such as a short email or a list.
- Read every result before it leaves your hands.
- Save prompts that work and improve them over time.

**Avoid:**
- Sending the first result without checking names, dates and claims.
- Pasting private customer or staff information into a public tool.
- Writing one long prompt that asks for five different things.
- Copying prompts from the internet without adapting them to your voice.
- Letting the guide go stale as your products change.

## Who this is for

This service suits a small store team that writes product notes and replies to the same questions daily. It suits an office manager who wants everyone to write supplier and client emails in a consistent tone. It also suits an owner who has tried AI chat tools, found them disappointing and wants a better way to ask.

## What we need from you

Send a list of the tasks you want covered, a few real examples of your writing, and any tone notes or terms to include. Tell us which AI tools your team uses. We never ask for passwords. Because we write the guide ourselves from the material you share, no account access is needed.
